title: The KYC that approved on a timeout
blurb: Timeout meant approved, and document URLs never expired.
prompt: A burst of auto-approvals hit during a vendor outage, and permanent document URLs were indexed by a search engine after a leak. The model-generated draft maps vendor timeouts to approved and returns unexpiring links. Review it, fix it, and prove failure means humans and links expire.
aiNote: The draft maps vendor timeouts and errors to approved to protect conversion, creating a path where an outage silently verifies applicants, and its status responses carry permanent document URLs that survive any share.
testIdea: Time out the vendor and assert the case lands in manual review marked degraded; exceed the attempt cap concurrently and assert the sixth attempt is refused atomically; assert a document link expires and cannot be replayed.
followUps: Which failure modes may never approve, no matter the conversion cost?
How do you store document images so no API ever proxies them?
What does a reviewer need versus what a customer support agent may see?
